column6: M: A proof of concept again. | F: And what is real? | M: The Modeller is, running in two windows. The pairing page and the little Team chip are a test bench. In daily work you would see only the chip.

column6: F: How do two windows become a team? | M: One starts a space, and its invite link stays hidden here. The other joins and shows a short code. The first window lists that same code and approves it. Then the second says enrolled. | F: And the phone? | M: Not needed this time. It is one fresh space for everything you see.

column6: M: Both windows start empty, with the Team chip in the corner. | F: And now? | M: A draws two blocks. Block one sits at x one, y a half. B still sees nothing.

column5: M: A visits. B visits, and both blocks appear.
column6: M: A visits, and a sealed letter goes in the post box. | F: And B? | M: B visits, and both blocks appear.

column5: F: What if both of us move something? | M: A drags block one left by two. B drags block two right by two.
column6: F: What if both of us move something? | M: A drags block one left by two. B drags block two right by two, before either visits. Each move is its own small letter, and different blocks never clash.

column4: LIVE · three Visits · §FILM_STATE moves_after_visits (identical on A and B)
column5: F: After the visits? | M: Both screens agree.
column6: F: And after the visits? | M: Both screens agree: block one at x minus one, block two at x five and a half.

column5: F: And the same block? | M: Then nobody silently wins.
column6: F: And the same block? | M: Then nobody silently wins. A drags block one a metre along x. B drags the same block two metres, before either has visited. | F: And then? | M: B also moves it a metre along y, a different direction.

column5: M: Both screens show the warning. The block stays put.
column6: M: Three visits, and now look. Both screens show the warning, naming both values, minus one and zero. | F: And the block? | M: It stays where they last agreed. The y move went through.

column4: LIVE · real gizmo drag: A x +1 · §FILM_DRAG · §FILM_STATE resolve_A_moved (A clear, B still warned)
column5: F: How does it end? | M: A moves it again.
column6: F: How does it end? | M: Someone who has seen both moves it again. A drags it one more metre.

column4: LIVE · two Visits · warning cleared · §FILM_STATE resolve_after_visits
column5: M: The warning clears on both.
column6: M: That counts as the decision. The warning is gone on both screens, and the block sits at x zero.

column5: F: Is everything shared? | M: No. Rotating stays local.
column6: F: Is everything shared? | M: No. A rotates the block, and the chip counts one local-only change. A's block is now one by two, while B's is still two by one.

column5: F: What is shared? | M: Only drawing and moving.
column6: F: So what is shared? | M: Only drawing and moving: seven of twenty-two operation types. Everything else stays on your device, and who may touch which floor or trade is still to be built.

column6: F: So, a shared model with no server? | M: A proof of concept, and every claim in it is backed by a test line. Same post office as the orders. Thanks for watching!
